To see the CLT in practice, adjust the sample size in the visualisation below.
The sampling distribution of the sample mean appears approximately normal as the sample size gets larger.



```{r, CLTDemo, echo=FALSE, fig.align="center", fig.cap="Exact sampling distribution of the mean (blue) overlaid with the CLT normal approximation (red dashed). The samples are drawn from a Gamma$(2, 1)$ distribution."}

# Gamma(alpha=2, rate=1): Xbar ~ Gamma(n*alpha, rate=n)
# mu = 2, sigma = sqrt(2)
alpha <- 2
beta  <- 1
mu    <- alpha / beta
sg    <- sqrt(alpha) / beta

ns <- c(1, 2, 5, 10, 30, 50, 100)

# Build x grid and densities for each n
traces <- lapply(ns, function(n) {
  se   <- sg / sqrt(n)
  x    <- seq(max(mu - 5*se, 1e-4), 
              mu + 5*se, 
              length.out = 600)
  yex  <- dgamma(x, 
                 shape = n * alpha, 
                 rate = n * beta)
  yclt <- dnorm(x,  
                mean  = mu,
                sd   = se)
  list(x = x, 
       yex = yex, 
       yclt = yclt, 
       n = n)
})

# Build figure
fig <- plot_ly(width = 600, 
               height = 400)

for (i in seq_along(ns)) {
  vis <- (i == 3)   # default: n = 5
  fig <- fig %>%
    add_lines(x = traces[[i]]$x, y = traces[[i]]$yex,
              visible    = vis,
              name       = "Exact",
              showlegend = (i == 1),
              line       = list(color = "steelblue", width = 2.5)) %>%
    add_lines(x = traces[[i]]$x, y = traces[[i]]$yclt,
              visible    = vis,
              name       = "CLT normal",
              showlegend = (i == 1),
              line       = list(color = "firebrick", width = 2, dash = "dash"))
}

# One button per n — each shows exactly 2 traces, hides all others
n_buttons <- lapply(seq_along(ns), function(i) {
  vis <- rep(FALSE, length(ns) * 2)
  vis[c(2*i - 1, 2*i)] <- TRUE
  list(
    method = "update",
    args   = list(
      list(visible = as.list(vis)),
      list(title  = paste0("Gamma(2, 1): sampling distribution of X\u0305,  n = ", ns[i]))
    ),
    label  = paste0("n = ", ns[i])
  )
})

fig <- fig %>% layout(
  title  = list(
    text = "Gamma(2, 1): sampling distribution of X\u0305,  n = 5",
    x = 0.5,
    xanchor = "center"),
  xaxis  = list(title = "x\u0305"),
  yaxis  = list(title = "Density"),
  margin = list(t = 60, 
                b = 110),
  legend = list(orientation = "h", 
                x = 0.65, 
                y = 1.0),
  updatemenus = list(
    list(
      type      = "buttons",
      direction = "right",
      x         = 0.0,
      y         = -0.28,
      xanchor   = "left",
      buttons   = n_buttons
    )
  )
) %>%
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE)

fig
```
